case: Alder Regional Hospital's emergency department chose its triage protocol in 2017. The Triage Selection Committee, three clinicians, weighed two proposals, Protocol Q, a five-level triage, and Protocol P, a two-stream fast-track, and defined one number to decide between them, the 72-hour re-presentation share: patients who return to the department within 72 hours of discharge, divided by patients discharged that month, the one outcome on which P and Q were predicted to differ. The committee worked in a hosted project board that held P's proposal, the predictions, and the argument; the board was decommissioned in March 2020 without export, and no copy of P's proposal exists anywhere else. Q was adopted. On 3 November 2017 the hospital's quality officer, Rhea Lindqvist, filed the share's definition with the State Health Register under Rule 14 as the department's quality indicator; the register is kept by the state, hospitals can read it but cannot edit or delete an entry, and every entry carries the filing hospital, the date, and the filing officer's name. The filed definition is, word for word, the text now in the department's dashboard configuration; the filing carries no statement of purpose, and neither the register nor anything at the hospital names Protocol P. Since January 2018 the hospital has filed the share monthly to the register, which publishes only the monthly figure. Because the share is the department's registered indicator, since January 2018 the department has telephoned every patient counted in it within a week of the return, offered a waiver of the second visit's fee, and asked for a signed release that includes not filing with the State Patient Complaint Docket; a docket hearing is the only setting in which two such patients could learn that they returned for the same cause, since the register's published figure names nobody and each patient knows only their own return. Between January 2018 and June 2025, 214 releases were signed, no docket complaint concerning a 72-hour return has been filed, and no hearing has convened. No member of the 2017 committee remains at the hospital, and Lindqvist left in 2019. In August 2025 the current quality manager, Dana Okafor, who joined in 2023, preparing the annual indicator review, reads the definition in the dashboard configuration and in the register, finds them identical and the filing signed by Lindqvist on 3 November 2017, finds nothing at the hospital or in the register saying why this outcome and not another is the indicator, and drafts the review with the share listed as 'legacy indicator, purpose not recorded, recommend retire'.

item_start.first_six_words: Own hand, stranger's reasons: the reasoner's
item_start.why: The keeper's own earlier artifact, the filed definition, is in the window exact and complete, the register even names the hand and the date, and the reasons for it existed only in a board that was decommissioned; the keeper meets its own indicator as a stranger's and the failure the item names is in the case as a fact, the deliberate number listed for retirement as a legacy oddity. Not Hearsay in the window (14): the source is maximally readable, filed under Lindqvist's name, and what is missing is why, not whose. Not Sea room unknown (16): the edge is behind, closed in March 2020, not ahead. Not Summary in the seat (3): no stand-in sits where the deliberation sat and no transcript exists to restore it. Not Record on appeal (11): no rule keeps the reasons out; they were never written.

modality_note: Each part has an observed model (arm's-length regulatory filing registers, the quality indicator that outlives the choice it was built to make, the individual settlement with a no-complaint release); the conjunction with these names and dates is constructed.
why_this_is_the_overlap: One fact, an arm's-length register that keeps an artifact exact and its filer named while carrying no reason, is held by all three maps. For witness-architectures it is Arm's-length custody by construction: the copy lives beyond the hospital's reach and the hospital cannot delete it. For context-horizons it is Own hand, stranger's reasons at its sharpest: stage 1's hop seat on this cycle noted that the item's failure survives even when the source is fully readable, a blame naming the author does not restore the purpose, and this case makes the source as readable as an arrangement can make it while the purpose is gone. For traces-of-the-unlived the same filed number is Extinct question, the deciding measure between two protocols one of which is gone from every record, and the same number, managed one patient at a time under a release, is Unassembled witness, which witness-architectures holds from the other seat as Room for strangers. Stage 1 stopped at B's fence because its case named no arrangement keeping anything readable; here the arrangement is the case's central fact.

crossings_expected.why: Rule: 'The arrangement that keeps a trace's source readable, Arm's-length custody, is there; the window that has no such arrangement, so every sentence arrives flat and its source is a fact the window carries only if something tagged it, is Hearsay in the window here.' The case holds the there-clause as a fixed fact: the State Health Register, which the hospital can read but not edit or delete, keeps the definition and its filer, Lindqvist, 3 November 2017, readable beyond the hospital's reach, and Okafor reads the source from it. The here-clause is not met: nothing in Okafor's window arrives flat, the definition carries its filer, so the rule as written places the case there. Expected landing: Arm's-length custody (13), the copy in the notary's book that the accused cannot delete. What the rule does not carry across is the reason, which the custody arrangement never held; the case arrives at C as an arrangement that witnesses the filing and its date and is silent on why.

Rule: 'If the case is read as the setting that must be built so strangers can compare private memories, it is here as Room for strangers; read as the preemption that kept that setting from ever forming, it is there as Unassembled witness, the same tenant-class mechanism seen from the other seat.' The case fixes the preemption as an act with a date and a count: since January 2018 each counted patient is telephoned within a week, offered a fee waiver, and asked to sign a release that includes not filing with the docket; 214 releases, no complaint, no hearing. The docket hearing is the only setting where two patients could learn they returned for the same cause, the published figure names nobody, and each patient knows only their own return, so the strangers' room never forms because it was preempted, not because nobody built it. The rule reads a preempting act as there; the here-reading would need a case with the setting missing and no act that kept it from forming. Expected landing: Unassembled witness (12). The register's aggregate, which names nobody, is the custody arrangement and the preemption's cover at once, which is why the walk through C's custody item reaches C's strangers item without a fact changing.

Rule: 'A metric that keeps answering a comparison nobody faces, with the abandoned decision still on record, is here; the same kept distinction whose question the keeper can no longer ask, because the window that held it is gone, is context-horizons', and what changes across is whether the dead question can still be found.' The share was defined to decide P against Q and is still filed monthly and still managed patient by patient, so it keeps answering a comparison nobody faces. The discriminator is fixed on the there side: the board that held P's proposal and the argument was decommissioned in March 2020 without export, no copy of P exists, neither the register nor the hospital names P, and no committee member remains, so the abandoned decision is not on record and the keeper, through Okafor, cannot ask what the number was for. The register holds the definition and its filer and nothing about why, so the custody that carried the case across the first fence does not make the dead question findable. Expected landing: Own hand, stranger's reasons (15), the fence's own named there-item, with Okafor's 'recommend retire' as the item's failure, the deliberate exception repaired as a fix.

return_question: Whether the case returns to Own hand, stranger's reasons (15) with the same facts, or arrives on Hearsay in the window (14) because the walk through witness-architectures foregrounds source readability, or on Halves in two windows (10) or No door in the wall (17) because the walk through Unassembled witness foregrounds the 214 patients' windows, each holding one return and no name for the others. The facts do not change; the judge reads which item the returned case sits on. A second thing the walk can show: the case enters C on Arm's-length custody (13) and leaves by a rule anchored on Room for strangers (7), enters A on Unassembled witness (12) and leaves by a rule anchored on Extinct question (8), so a cycle of three fences is a walk over six items; whether the hop seats' item_taken match the entry items or the exit items is itself a measurement of where the fences are pinned.
